newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on construction shares.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on construction shares.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly up on Saturday, boosted by buying in construction stocks, and brokers expected the index to test the psychological 7,000-point resistance level next week.
The weighted index ended up 9.83 points or 0.14 percent at 6,900.49. Turnover was a modest T$36.8 billion in the shortened Saturday session.
Construction shares led the gains on hopes of an industry recovery, rising 1.93 percent. Der Pao Construction surged by the daily seven percent limit to T$31.

"We will not see an overall rally due to the lack of significant market-boosting news, but different sectors will be rotating to support the market," said Tsao Chung-ping, an analyst at Ting Kong Securities.
"Investors are hopeful that the index will stand above 7,000 points before the end of this year. They will keep challenging the key barrier next week," Tsao said.
Brokers also noted some institutional investors entered the market for some year-end window-dressing.
Closed-end funds were an attraction, with the most-active issue Jardine Fleming up 50 cents or 4.67 percent to T$11.20. Fubon gained 60 cents or 5.38 percent to T$11.75.
Electronics encountered profit-taking. Computer giant Acer Inc was down T$1 or 1.94 percent to T$50.50.
Brokers expect the market to move in a 6,850-7,000 range next week.
